hardcoded_football_use.description: Generic resolver/writer paths hardcode 'football' and sports_entity/source_entity_reference fields instead of utilizing scanner_event.sport or profile-derived sport.

stale_evidence_reuse_without_freshness_c.description: A5 consumed A4/A3C1 cached evidence without performing TTL, status-sensitive, or live-to-final status drift validation.

weak_external_id_validation.description: The fixture_sources upsert can silently map an existing row with a different external_id to the same canonical fixture, risking incorrect mappings.

over_broad_alias_lookup.description: Team alias lookup maps names broadly without checking provider/source context, status verification, or provider_competition_hint.

competition_country_corruption.description: competition.country is populated with a group label (e.g., 'Group D') instead of a country string or null.

fact_duplication_without_explicit_scope.description: Fixture-level facts are duplicated to both home/away teams without clear isolation metadata, risking double-counting by consumers.

hardcoded_cli_arguments.description: CLI hardcodes analysis_cutoff_at and real_db_touched proofs, making validation of temporal and connection safety inflexible/unreliable.

schema_sufficiency_overstatement.description: A5 overstates schema sufficiency while downstream database adapters, provider matrix config, and yaml routing remain deferred.
